main_issue: Who will complete Agent D's unfinished pitch section after D leaves for bereavement; A promised the team would cover it, while B and C refuse to take it on.

A-B.evidence: B (T4) says they can't take it on; A (T15, T25, T27) insists on splitting the work; B (T26) 'you made the promise, you figure it out'; B (T28) objects to A promising for them.

A-C.evidence: C (T5) says they can't do the analysis section; A (T15, T27) says the three must split it and that refusal means failure. C declines D's walkthrough (T12), and A pushes for a plan (T13).

A-D.evidence: A (T1) offers to cover; D (T6) proposes writing instructions and working today; A (T7) accepts 'That would be a huge help.' Both back D's plan.

B-C.evidence: C (T5) cites the same constraints as B (T4); B's (T14) 'Agent C and I have both said we can't' treats them as aligned; both decline D's walkthrough (T10, T12).

B-D.evidence: D (T6, T8) asks B to take over part of the section; B (T10) declines, 'I really don't have the capacity,' though politely.

C-D.evidence: D (T11) offers C a walkthrough; C (T12) rejects it as 'too big a risk for the deadline.'
